originalTitle: SPMO Owns the S&P 500’s 100 Fastest-Rising Stocks. Its Momentum Screen Has Beaten the Index by 67-Points Over the Last Five Years
summary: A simple momentum screen applied to S&P 500 stocks has quietly built a performance gap that turns identical starting portfolios into dramatically different ending balances, and the strategy costs almost nothing to implement.
content:
A simple momentum screen applied to S&P 500 stocks has quietly built a performance gap that turns identical starting portfolios into dramatically different ending balances, and the strategy costs almost nothing to implement.

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Owning the S&P 500 has proven to be one of the simplest ways to build wealth over the long-term. But one ETF has taken the same pool of large-cap stocks, applied a momentum screen, and produced substantially better results over the last five years. The Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF ( NYSEARCA:SPMO ) has returned 137.81% cumulatively over the last five years, working out to just shy of 20% annualized. By comparison, the S&P 500 has returned 70.27% over the same period, or approximately 13% annualized. This momentum-driven performance advantage results in two portfolios with drastically different ending values.

SPMO does one thing, and it does it very well – momentum.

SPMO does not venture into small-cap stocks, obscure technology companies, or speculative names looking for the next market winner. Rather, it starts with companies already included in the S&P 500 and tracks the S&P 500 Momentum Index.

The index selects roughly 100 stocks with the strongest momentum scores and reconstitutes and rebalances twice per year, in March and September. The idea behind the strategy is straightforward: stocks that have demonstrated stronger recent relative performance may continue outperforming.

Constituents are then weighted using both market capitalization and their momentum scores. SPMO charges an expense ratio of just 0.13%, or roughly $13 annually for every $10,000 invested.

That process currently produces a portfolio that looks considerably different from a traditional S&P 500 fund. Based on current holdings, technology represents roughly 54% of the fund. Names like Micron Technology alone account for more than 11% of assets. Meanwhile, Nvidia represents roughly 9%, followed by Broadcom at more than 6%. Johnson & Johnson, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet, and Lam Research are also among its largest positions. Altogether, the top 10 stocks represented just more than half of the portfolio.

The Five-Year Performance Gap Is Hard to Ignore

The results have been impressive. Through August 31, SPMO delivered a five-year annualized return of 19.7%, compared with 12.8% for the S&P 500 Total Return Index. Over three years, the difference was even larger: SPMO returned 37.3% annually compared with 21.0% for the index. The fund has also been ahead in 2026 through August, returning 23.8% against 13.1% for the S&P 500.

Put these numbers into dollars, and the difference becomes easier to appreciate. A hypothetical $100,000 compounded at 19.7% annually for five years grows to roughly $246,000. At 12.8%, the same starting balance grows to about $183,000. That is a difference of more than $60,000 without leaving the universe of stocks already found in the S&P 500.

Momentum Comes with a Different Kind of Risk

While it is tempting to project past results forward, there is no guarantee that the advantage will continue. Momentum strategies naturally concentrate money in stocks and sectors that have already performed well. Today that means heavy exposure to semiconductors and technology. If leadership changes quickly, SPMO can find itself holding yesterday’s winners while the rest of the market rotates elsewhere.

The fund also turns over more aggressively than a plain S&P 500 ETF because the index needs to continually identify new momentum leaders. According to Morningstar, the fund has a recent portfolio turnover of 44%. Investors should therefore view SPMO as more than a slightly modified S&P 500 fund. Its portfolio can become substantially more concentrated, and its results can diverge sharply from the broad index in either direction.

SPMO has taken roughly 100 stocks from the same S&P 500 universe and generated a significant performance advantage over the past five years. Investors comfortable with greater concentration and the possibility of sharp changes in market leadership may find that paying 0.13% for a systematic momentum screen offers a compelling alternative to simply owning all 500 stocks. For those simply looking for S&P 500 exposure, standard index funds still prove to be an effective way to compound wealth over time.

chineseTitle: SPMO 拥有标准普尔 500 指数中上涨最快的 100 只股票。过去 5 年，其动量屏幕跑赢指数 67 点
chineseSummary: 应用于标准普尔 500 指数股票的简单动量筛选已悄然建立了绩效差距，将相同的起始投资组合转变为截然不同的期末余额，而且该策略的实施成本几乎为零。
chineseContent:
应用于标准普尔 500 指数股票的简单动量筛选已悄然建立了绩效差距，将相同的起始投资组合转变为截然不同的期末余额，而且该策略的实施成本几乎为零。

这篇文章可能包含来自我们的赞助商和附属机构的链接，Flywheel Publishing 可能会因通过他们采取的行动而获得报酬。

事实证明，持有标准普尔 500 指数是长期积累财富的最简单方法之一。但一只 ETF 选取了同一组大盘股，应用了动量筛选，并在过去五年中产生了明显更好的结果。 Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF (NYSEARCA:SPMO) 过去五年累计回报率为 137.81%，年化回报率略低于 20%。相比之下，标准普尔 500 指数同期回报率为 70.27%，年化回报率约为 13%。这种动量驱动的绩效优势导致两个投资组合的最终价值截然不同。

SPMO 做了一件事，而且做得非常好——动量。

SPMO 不会涉足小盘股、默默无闻的科技公司或寻找下一个市场赢家的投机公司。相反，它从已纳入 S&P 500 指数的公司开始，并跟踪 S&P 500 动量指数。

该指数选择大约 100 只动量得分最强的股票，并每年在 3 月和 9 月进行两次重组和重新平衡。该策略背后的想法很简单：近期相对表现强劲的股票可能会继续跑赢大盘。

然后使用市值及其动量得分对成分股进行加权。 SPMO 的费用率仅为 0.13%，即每投资 10,000 美元每年大约收取 13 美元。

目前，这一流程产生的投资组合与传统的标准普尔 500 指数基金有很大不同。根据目前的持有量，科技股约占该基金的 54%。仅美光科技这样的公司就占资产的 11% 以上。与此同时，Nvidia 的市场份额约为 9%，其次是 Broadcom，市场份额超过 6%。强生公司、Advanced Micro Devices、Alphabet 和 Lam Research 也是其最大的仓位之一。总共，前 10 名股票仅占投资组合的一半以上。

五年绩效差距难以忽视

结果令人印象深刻。截至 8 月 31 日，SPMO 的五年年化回报率为 19.7%，而标准普尔 500 总回报指数为 12.8%。三年来，差异甚至更大：SPMO 的年回报率为 37.3%，而该指数的年回报率为 21.0%。该基金在 2026 年至 8 月份期间也一直处于领先地位，回报率为 23.8%，而标准普尔 500 指数的回报率为 13.1%。

将这些数字换算成美元，差异就会变得更容易理解。假设 100,000 美元，五年内每年复合增长率为 19.7%，将增长到大约 246,000 美元。初始余额为 12.8%，增长至约 183,000 美元。如果不考虑标准普尔 500 指数中已有的股票范围，这一差异将超过 60,000 美元。

势头伴随着不同类型的风险

虽然人们很容易预测过去的结果，但并不能保证这种优势会持续下去。动量策略自然会将资金集中在已经表现良好的股票和板块上。如今，这意味着大量接触半导体和技术。如果领导层迅速更换，SPMO 可能会发现自己持有昨天的赢家，而市场的其余部分则转向其他地方。

该基金的换手率也比普通标普 500 ETF 更积极，因为该指数需要不断寻找新的动能领导者。据晨星公司称，该基金最近的投资组合换手率为 44%。因此，投资者不应将 SPMO 视为稍微修改过的标准普尔 500 指数基金。其投资组合可能会变得更加集中，其结果可能会在任一方向上与广泛指数产生巨大差异。

SPMO 从同一标准普尔 500 指数中选取了大约 100 只股票，并在过去五年中产生了显着的业绩优势。对更大的集中度和市场领导力发生急剧变化的可能性感到满意的投资者可能会发现，支付 0.13% 的系统动量筛选费用是简单地拥有全部 500 只股票的一个令人信服的选择。对于那些只是寻求标普 500 指数投资的人来说，标准指数基金仍然被证明是随着时间的推移实现财富复合的有效方式。
